indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.2.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of the life cycle of plants

skills.description: Name common seeds found in the environment
Match a seed to the fruit or plant it comes from
Draw and label one or two seeds observed

misconceptions: A seed is the same as a fruit.
Only big seeds can grow into plants.
Confusing 'seed' with 'nut' or 'stone' in everyday language.

questions.stem: Which of these is a seed?
hints: You plant it to grow a new plant.
It can be cooked and eaten.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any small object is a seed.

questions.stem: Where do we find the seed of an orange?
questions.explanation: The seed of an orange is found inside the fruit.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds grow outside the fruit.

questions.stem: Which of these seeds is eaten as a snack in Ghana?
questions.explanation: Groundnut is a seed that is commonly eaten as a snack.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know that groundnuts are seeds.

questions.stem: Which seed comes from a maize plant?
questions.explanation: The corn seed (maize) grows on a cob.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse corn with other yellow foods.

questions.stem: Are all seeds the same size?
options: Only the ones in the ground
hints: Compare a mango seed and a bean seed.
Some are big, some are small.
questions.explanation: No, seeds come in different sizes. A mango seed is big, and a bean seed is smaller.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all seeds look alike.

questions.stem: Which fruit has a large, hard seed in the middle?
hints: The seed is big and flat.
questions.explanation: The mango has a large, hard seed in the middle.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think bananas have large seeds.

questions.stem: How is a maize seed different from a bean seed?
options: The maize seed is yellow and the bean seed is red/brown
The maize seed is small and the bean seed is huge
hints: What colour is a typical bean?
questions.explanation: Maize seeds are usually yellow or white, while bean seeds are often red, brown, or black.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all seeds are brown.

options: Inside fruits and in the soil
questions.explanation: Seeds are found inside fruits and in the soil (after planting).
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize seeds come from fruits.

questions.stem: Ama has an orange seed and a groundnut. How are they different?
options: The orange seed is inside a fruit and the groundnut is a seed we eat
The groundnut is inside an orange
The orange seed is big and hard
hints: Where do you find each one?
Can you eat a groundnut directly?
questions.explanation: An orange seed is found inside the orange fruit, while a groundnut is a seed we can eat directly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the difference between a seed inside a fruit and a seed we eat.

questions.stem: Name one seed you can find in your home.
questions.explanation: Seeds like beans, maize, and groundnuts are commonly found in homes.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name rice, but rice is also a seed; accept it.

questions.stem: What fruit does a pawpaw seed come from?
hints: It has many small black seeds.
questions.explanation: A pawpaw seed comes from a pawpaw fruit.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know what a pawpaw is.

questions.stem: Kwame has two seeds. Seed A is very small. Seed B is large and hard. Which could be a mango seed?
questions.explanation: Mango seeds are large and hard, so Seed B is likely the mango seed.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think small seeds are the only ones that grow.

questions.stem: Why do some seeds have a hard outer cover?
questions.explanation: The hard outer cover protects the inside of the seed.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the hard cover is just for decoration.

questions.stem: Which of these statements is TRUE?
options: Seeds can grow into new plants
Seeds do not need soil to grow
hints: What happens when you plant a seed?
questions.explanation: Seeds can grow into new plants when planted.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think seeds are just food and do not grow.

questions.stem: Draw a bean seed and a maize seed. Write 'bean' under the bean and 'maize' under the maize.
hints: Maize is like a small yellow tooth.
questions.explanation: This tests observation and drawing of two different seeds.

questions.stem: Name two seeds that you can eat and two seeds that you cannot eat.

criteria.description: Names one non-edible seed (e.g., mango seed, orange seed)

hints: Think about mango and orange seeds.
questions.explanation: Beans and groundnuts are edible. Mango and orange seeds are usually not eaten.

questions.stem: A farmer plants a maize seed. What will grow from it?
hints: The seed comes from the maize plant.
It grows into the same kind of plant.
questions.explanation: A maize seed grows into a maize plant.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a seed can grow into any plant.

questions.stem: Look at a mango seed and a bean seed. Write one way they are different.

criteria.description: States a valid difference (e.g., size, colour, hardness)

questions.explanation: A mango seed is larger and harder than a bean seed.

questions.stem: Draw a pawpaw seed and a groundnut. Colour them.

criteria.description: Draws a small black pawpaw seed

hints: Pawpaw seeds are small and black.
questions.explanation: This tests observation of seed colour and size.
